problem: The CoBuilder workflows consult Hindsight only through an optional build step. Three of 15 build plans opted in, and design mode never consults memory. The Hindsight Stop hook writes each transcript back as chat. Only an opted-in build writes a decision on its own, so recall returns mostly raw chat. The automatic memory folder never reaches Hindsight.
why_now: Claude Code 2.1.296 ships function hooks. A plugin can now run a small model at every prompt and stop. It can also fork the conversation, call an MCP server, and add a note that the model reads. Before this, memory ran only when the model chose to call it.
approach: A new opt-in plugin, cobuilder-memory, ships one hooks module. A Haiku router labels each person prompt and each stop: read none, recall, or reflect, and write none or retain. A label starts a quick run: a conversation fork writes a JSON recall plan, and the module makes each Hindsight call. Fixed workflow moments call the plugin's moment tool, which starts a deep run: a fork agent with read-only tools recalls and checks each claim. The module runs the cc-memory-mirror, appends one memory note, and writes one receipt per run. A spike tests the open facts first.

alternatives.option: Fixed moments and the cc-memory-mirror only, with no router
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer wants memory at ordinary prompts and at every stop. Without a router, a prompt between two workflow moments gets no memory.

alternatives.option: A deep run for every trigger
alternatives.rejected_because: Each step of a fork agent reads the cached session again. A run at every prompt multiplies that cost.

alternatives.option: A quick run for every trigger, workflow moments included
alternatives.rejected_because: A fork from $.model.fork has no tools. It cannot check a claim in the repo or ask a follow-up query, and workflow moments feed design decisions (D2).

alternatives.option: Keep the opt-in H1 to H5 checkpoints with fixed query text
alternatives.rejected_because: Three of 15 build plans opted in. Fixed text asks the same question at every gate, and the engineer retired it (D1).

alternatives.option: Detect the design and build starts with a command.run hook
alternatives.rejected_because: No test shows that command.run fires for a plugin's markdown command. An explicit tool call at a named workflow step is testable and survives a renamed command.

alternatives.option: Add cobuilder-memory to the umbrella plugin
alternatives.rejected_because: The plugin adds model calls at every prompt and writes to memory. A person must choose both, not get them as a side effect of the family install.

alternatives.option: Copy the CLAUDE.md files into Hindsight as well
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer chose the automatic memory folder (M1 b). CLAUDE.md files live in git, where review already governs each change.
A receipt comes with every routed prompt, so committed receipts would bury real changes. A committed memory citation carries the run id and the memory id instead.
One low-budget reflect on this 544-fact bank used 74,764 input tokens on the Hindsight server. A run allows one reflect, on a reflect label or in a deep run.

alternatives.option: Recall with the default observation type
alternatives.rejected_because: This bank holds no observations, so an observation-only recall returns nothing. Every recall sets the world and experience types.
The bank already tags extracted facts knowledge:decision. A second tag would give one kind two names.

alternatives.option: Rename the plugin to memory, as the ADR-0016 addendum rule says
alternatives.rejected_because: A bare name collides with the built-in /memory command. Its tools would also share the mcp__memory__ prefix of the common memory MCP server.

alternatives.option: A quick run with no fork, and the trimmed prompt as the query
alternatives.rejected_because: The queries lose the session context. It is faster and cheaper, and the engineer chose context.

alternatives.option: The prompt and stop hooks wait for the quick run, with no queue and no timer
alternatives.rejected_because: The person's prompt would wait for the router and the run. The engineer chose that a note never waits (M3 a).

out_of_scope: Any change to the Hindsight server, the hindsight-coding-agents runtime, or its three settings hooks.
The review, maintenance, options, debug, and pr modes. They make no memory call in this design.
An MCP server, an agent file, or a slash command of the plugin's own.
A copy of CLAUDE.md files, or of any file outside the automatic memory folder.
The 0.90 accept rule in slice-loop.md. It stays an open question outside this design.
risks: The hooks API is early access and changes between releases. Each engine call sits behind one adapter module, and spike S10 records the build it ran on.
The router adds two small model calls to every exchange, and each recall label adds one fork that reads the cached session. Each receipt records both.
A retain writes a wrong decision at once (M2 a). A toast shows it, and the receipt keeps the memory id, so a person can invalidate the record.
A fork agent inherits write tools. A tool.call guard denies each call outside its allow-list. If the spike shows the guard fails, the deep run holds no tools (R2-2 a).
A memory note could flow back into the bank. The Stop hook skips isMeta rows and strips the hindsight_memories tag, and a done_when item tests it.
Hindsight is down or not installed. The router stays quiet while Hindsight does not answer, and the module checks again at each stop. A workflow moment writes a gap line.
Recall returns this session's own transcript. The module drops each result whose document id is conversation plus this session id.
One reflect costs about 75,000 input tokens on the Hindsight server. A session allows three reflects, and each receipt counts them.
testing: The spike runs the eleven checks in spike.md on Claude Code 2.1.296. `claude plugin test` runs the module's tests with model, fork, and MCP answers mocked beneath it. `uv run pytest tests -q` checks the packaging rule. A live run in this repo checks one routed prompt, one stop, one workflow moment, and one cc-memory-mirror change.
reviewer_focus: The install-surface amendment: does ADR-0039 keep agents/ for implement alone, and MCP servers forbidden for every plugin?
The quick-run handover: does the fork prompt carry the trigger, the labels, and the new prompt, and nothing the fork already sees?
The deep-run guard: does its allow-list hold read tools only?
unknowns: Does command.run fire for the built-in /memory, and does next(e) resolve when the person closes it?
Does a hooks module's classic.Stop hook fire at every stop, a /goal iteration included, while turn.complete fires once per turn?
Does a fork from $.agent.spawn report each tool call to the mod's tool.call hook with its agent id?
Does a plugin-spawned fork's final answer reach the main conversation, or must the module append it?
Do $.model.fork and $.mcp.call run from a timer that session.start started, and how much of the prefix does the cache serve?
Does a retain with the same document_id replace the earlier document?
Does a recall after a stop find no text of a memory note or of a deep-run result in the bank?
Can the module find the automatic memory folder from the context's AutoMem entry?
Does prompt.submit mark the person's own prompt with origin kind composer, and does a subagent's stop carry a field that names the agent?
Does each $ call and event that ADR-0039 names exist in the build that ships, and does the shipped plugin layout load the hook?
